title: Secession Building
subtitle: Must a fork always be paired with a cake? Must art always adhere to tradition?

content.text: Look at this, dearie. This kind of hand mirror has become the latest fashion. Oh, it's a trifling thing, but people like me have to stay in the loop to make a living.
Come here. Gaze into the mirror, and fix your hat. What do you see? Do you like what you see?
I feel as if I can see all of Vienna.

branch.text: A clever answer! I can tell you will fit right in here.
But there is still much left to see beyond the mirror. Oh. The young folk step to an ever-changing waltz. If you want to follow their trends, you'll need perfect timing to join the swirling dance.

Some have fallen behind. They lounge by the fountains of the park, bemoaning their lives and the price of rent. Come the next banquet and exhibition, they arrive wearing a new fine coat, but underneath their linens are ragged and old.
The mirror's reflection held a silver sheen once. Now it's tarnished at the edges.
Oh, look at our little artist in the mirror.
Something of a narcissist, then? No, I'm not laughing at you. In this place, valuing one's uniqueness, one's own voice is much to be desired.
You have to be loud enough, firm enough to show no fear, nor hesitation. So that at the end of the waltz, you will have the strength to break their instruments.
Is that so? Oh, has something gone wrong? Did an old lady like me waste her money?
Or, perhaps what it reflects is the "truth."
The mirror shows reality, nothing more, nothing less. So, it may be that there is nothing to see, or it may be something that can't be seen.
But things change, darling, especially in this city. Like an avalanche taking everything in its path, changing them irrecoverably and inevitably.
So next time when you look into a mirror like this, you may just see something else. Be patient.
So, in the warmth of spring, the ice cracks deeper. One splinters into two, and each begins to splinter again.
They set up the mirror and lift the cloth exposing to light—the good, the bad, and what lies beyond them both.
Then the factions split and then split again. "Secessionists," by their nature, are not in the business of keeping things together. They won't stop the fractures—they can't.
In lifting the cloth and seeing their reflection, they scatter themselves like dandelion seeds in the wind.

Oh, I don't know where, but I do know what they're doing. Some of them still paint with gold leaf, others believe they must depict what is real, some depict the ravings of their dreams, some seek to change the streets into works of art, and others drive out all meaning from their work.
The only time they ever reach an agreement is just before they lift the cloth from the mirror.
Before the Potemkin village with all its empty facades moves somewhere else, some of them might just achieve their ends.
To be like the golden cabbage sitting atop its dome over the Ring Road—to be recognized by everyone.

items.text: Secession Building

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: So this ... is the Vienna branch?!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: It's ... splendid! Look at the walls, simple yet elegant ... It's like a temple of modern art!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Hmm, I can read ... the contrast between different shapes and textures ... This Mr. Olbrich must have put so much effort into the design.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: It must be a very pleasant place to work at, Mr. Karl!

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Huh? Oh no, this is the Secession Building.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Another meeting place for the young artists to show off, other than the cafes. They said they wanted to break away from traditional art. Well, it's more like they're breaking away from human life.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: There's nothing to like here, only inexplicable paintings and neurasthenic lunatics, but people keep coming back. There are even secession groups to the secession, like cells dividing through mitosis.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: The entrance to our venerable branch is on the left. Please follow me ...
A massive golem stands at the door, towering over the approaching trio.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Notice the guard? It's the most loyal and reliable knight of Vienna, powered entirely by arcane ritual. The greatest achievement since the revival of arcanum in Europe!

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: In 1662, a royal magician from London offered it to the Emperor at the time. Since then, it's guarded the Empire for centuries ...
Ah, sir!
A figure emerges from within the shadow of the golem.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... Hmm?

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Greetings, dear Sir Scarpia! How is your son Tamino? I hear he's not getting along well with his fiancee.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: He's a strange one. What's he doing standing in a corner like that?

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: ... My apologies, Ms. Hofmann. Please hold on.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Terrific, Heinrich, just as terrific as your pathetic art career.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: That's great! Best wishes to you, Sir Scarpia!

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Oh, my apologies.
He stands in the distance, giving a nod towards Hofmann and Marcus.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Greetings to you, Angelotti, and ... Unknown Lady.
The gentleman turns and moves briskly into the temple-like edifice, as peculiar in his exit as he was in his entrance.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: See, he is one of those crazy artists. Everyone knows that I only have this beautiful daughter of mine! This mustacheless gentleman went to study in Berlin and has just returned.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: I guess he didn't learn much in class, and now he's throwing himself into opera ...

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: He must've listened to Wagner and Mozart so much it damaged his central nervous system. That's why he sees everyone as a character in an opera.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Operas and music, they do harm to your eyes and fill your ears with useless sounds ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Is every artist like this?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Hmm, Scarpia, Angelotti ... They are indeed characters from the opera Tosca.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Oops, I am getting off topic.
Karl's cane raps on the stone creature in front of him.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Don't worry. We've modified its original ritual to meet the needs here. Lots of people come in and out, after all.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: You just need to knock on the armor three times, touch your mustache, and it will let you in.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: I forgot you have no mustaches, my dear ladies! But you do have ... arcane skills, right?

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: First of all, I'm not an arcanist.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Second, I'm not as humorous as you think.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Fine! But that was no joke. This thing only accepts mustaches. It's a symbol that every gentleman should have ... And not everyone's like Heinrich!
The absurdity seems to have finally broken the senior investigator's patience.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Just give me the list of arcanists we mentioned in the letter, Mr. Karl. We don't need to go into the branch.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Oh, no. Do you really want to miss the scenery of the Danube? And the sight of the modern transport system? There's no better way to tour the Ring Road than by carriage! And we've booked a room for you at the Sacher hotel ...

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: By the way, have you tried the treasure of Austria?

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Thank you, we already had it while you were enjoying your lunch.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Now, please. Give us, the list.
Hofmann's tone marks the request as non-negotiable.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: And I'm sure you've received a telegram from the headquarters. You are to investigate the people around Theophil von Dittarsdorf.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Ok. Alright, it's a pity, lady from the headquarters.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Here you are ... And that's all of it, all of it!

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Oh, and this ...

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Two tickets to the Vienna Court Opera. Please give them to Mr. Richard, and when you see him ... send my sincerest regards.
Hofmann stands still, maintaining a distant politeness.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I will.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... Who's Mr. Richard?

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The contact between the Foundation and the Vienna branch in 1914 ... a phantom of history.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: At that time, people still believed the golden age that had begun with the last generation would continue as it should, and that their positions in government would be as unshakable as the long-standing Empire.
Hofmann nods, watching as old Karl taps his cane and strokes his beard, before disappearing into the corridor opened by the golem.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: ... Hmm? Shoot. It won't let me in!

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: You're not joking are you, Mr. Karl?

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: I am not! Darn. What is going on? Is this thing broken?

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Ugh, I'm stuck ... My belly! I had this suit custom-made in Paris!
The ancient knight awakens in a slow stir, shaking off a heavy layer of dust as thick as a Viennese title.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: What on earth is going on?! Why is the defense system activated?!
A comical voice emanates from within the statue, lilting and quick, like a rubber ball bouncing around inside a hollow frame.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: *sighs*

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Marcus, can you "read" its internal rituals?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Hmm, considering its sluggishness ... yes, I think so.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Good.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: It's a good chance for you to get some experience. Just stay safe.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: Oh no! Ms. Hofmann, these golems represent the spirit of the Vienna branch ... You shouldn't be so violent ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Adapt, improve, and advance. Arcanum should be kept up with the times, not lock itself away in a museum and wallow in the good old days.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: There was something visibly wrong with this thing, and we were rightfully doing our job. If you have any concerns about this, I'll include them in the report.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: And I should remind you that you've spent too much time on your ... free will. We're running out of time.

items.speaker: Karl
items.text: No, no, procedures are not the problem! Darn it ... you're not German, are you?
The division head mutters softly, before proceeding inside at last.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: So what's wrong with the golem?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Hmm, as Mr. Karl said, its structure is simple and yet incredible ... The malfunction comes from one of the components. There's an extra stroke on the enchantment.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: These strokes look new. I guess the staff made a mistake when they did the maintenance or repair.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Let's hope so.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Now take a look at this before Mr. Karl comes out.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Several days ago, a member of the Field Agent Squad found a painting that was reported in this magazine, the Pan.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: It belonged to Theophil von Dittarsdorf, a deceased artist from Vienna who committed suicide.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Its name is The Salvation, and it was found along with a poem.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The poem mentioned the "doomsday," the "reversal of time," and the "rain."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... Salvation and rain? It sounds so ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Yes. And given the sightings of Manus leaders in Vienna ...

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: We believe Theophil came into contact with Manus leaders before he died, and probably learned the truth of the "Storm" and the method of "salvation."

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: This was how Manus Vindictae recruited arcanists in 1929.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Hmm ... If he knew the method of "salvation," why did he still kill himself?
Marcus takes the magazine with ready curiosity, looking at the small, clipped section.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Seeking Silenus in the woods, I asked him,"

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "What is the best and most wonderful thing for man?"

items.speaker: Marcus & Isolde
items.text: "'The emptiness where man was never born!' He said."

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: "I looked at it, the ring of life, the ring of all lives."

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: "Your hands form the ring, and the judgment is pronounced."

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: "On the doomsday, at the dusk when history fades away."

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: "Oh world! Its head bites its feet, its knees touch its nose."

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: "Oh man! They inhabit the earth, waiting for the sky to fall."

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: "Yesterday turns into tomorrow, tomorrow reverts to yesterday."

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: "Who shall vanish in the rain?"

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: "Who shall be granted the eternal happiness, the grace from above—"

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: "And that emptiness, the cessation of existence?"
Secession Building

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: That was so moving, Ms. Sieglinde.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Poor Siegmund, my best friend, has returned to the void. Thank you all for coming today to shed tears for our departed hero.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: He was a righteous and noble man who cared for his people. He was still trying to save the arcanists on the Golden Isle before he died. He left us so many beautiful poems and paintings.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Shame that the fire burned everything to ashes. The only thing that survived was ... The Salvation.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: We were in a golden age of progressive ideas. We believed the Enlightenment would make ignorance history and lead us to paradise, where everyone would be saved ...

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: The barrier between arcanists and humans would be removed. In Vienna, that tolerant city, we would stand together, hand in hand, back to back, reliving the intimacy we once shared when we first came into this world.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: "Oh world! Its head bites its feet, its knees touch its nose."

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: But the reality is, the survival space of arcanists is shrinking. We try to speak up in our own language, but that only makes us strangers in our own land.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: That's why we have decided to exhibit Siegmund's last work, not only in memory of the deceased ...

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: ... but in memory of his noble spirit, his sincere concern for his people, and his scrutiny of this tragic world.
The people gathered nod their heads. Some of the women begin to weep softly.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: There is no need to be sad, my friends! He has left us with the Rhinegold!

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: We will found a committee with the funds raised by the exhibition to improve the conditions of unregistered arcanists.

items.speaker: Guest I
items.text: The youngest and most outstanding opera singer in Vienna, Theophil's sister, Isolde von Dittarsdorf, will present the details.
Amidst applause, Heinrich bows, handing off the stage to its true protagonist.
She takes a graceful step forward.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Now I see ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... why we were ordered to investigate Theophil's connections.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: There may be spies from Manus Vindictae among them.
Her mentor nods in approval, handing over a stack of documents.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I know the Vienna branch has a lot of bureaucratic problems, but we need their help to carry out the mission in this era.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: The search warrant, the letter of introduction, the evidence collection permit ... They've provided us with all the official documents we need in this era, as well as the list of all the arcanists in Vienna in 1914.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: But we're not going to cooperate with them any further, because of the requirements to confidentiality. We'll only need manpower from them in the following operations.
Marcus replies by opening the thick register of arcanists. Desperate to prove she hasn't gotten distracted this time.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: ... In case you spend a whole day on the "A" section, Marcus, we're looking for "Theophil," starts with a "T."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: H-How did you know I was starting from line A ...
The apprentice droops her shoulders, sinking back into the book. With the help of her arcane skill, she easily finds the information that Hofmann seeks.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: It says Theophil belonged to a group of artists called "The Circle."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: They often gathered in the Secession Building. Madam Hofmann, I think we can make contact with them one by one ...
Ahh!

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: What's happening?!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Erm, I sense strong arcane fluctuations over there!
Her eyes center on the door of the Secession Building.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I think it's ... it's a ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... ghost?
TO BE CONTINUED…
